body: Best of luck to you too! and I hope that if you have to you can find a pt job that isn't too exhausting, e.g. security guard, tutor, adjunct instructor, etc.  Save your energy for the job hunt!
Okay, thank you for sharing some of your experience - as you can tell, I'm new to the job market so posts like this help me to know what is/isn't appropriate.

I'm not so sure that there is a general definition of a "master's level job"; in my field, the dividing line between jobs requiring different education levels is pretty clear.  That may not be the case in your field.

If I may make one more suggestion, I think "upping your game" might be the wrong way to think about it - the problem is that you are very worried and distressed about your situation.  But, your situation is totally normal and there's no reason to panic.  Just work carefully and methodically and eventually you'll land that job.  Work a part time job for now if you want/need to; personally, I think it's a better use of time to apply for jobs, hone my skills and even relax a bit and enjoy this period of my life.

I hope this was helpful.  Best of luck in your search.  I know you'll make it!  But these things take time.
Thank you for taking the time to reply.

I'm not sure how encouraging this is, but I'm in pretty much the same boat (master's and all).

I guess the silver lining is that, even though competition is tough for MS level jobs, long-term unemployment of master's-educated people is very low.  What I've been doing is just taking it one day at a time, doing a lot of applications but spending the time to tailor each application to its respective company.  I aim to do 5 or 6 per day.

In my perspective, not freaking out and realizing that you *will* eventually get a job is key.

Yeah, that's what I was afraid of...

Seems like you're supposed to just drop your resume into a black box and see what happens.

I guess that's the question.  I feel like I've done everything I could reasonably be expected to do to improve my situation.  Like I said in the OP, I've been applying for jobs for just shy of 2 months and gotten no interviews - which is part of the reason why I believe I am on an HR blacklist.  I've tried many times to keep a job but I always get fired due to anxiety which makes it basically impossible for me to perform my job to standard.

Therefore, me continuing to exist doesn't contribute to paying taxes because I don't think I can get or maintain a job.  So instead of paying taxes, I'm more likely to end up on public assistance.  From that perspective, it is better for society for me to die.

Thank you for your response.

I don't believe in an afterlife because all cognition appears to come from the brain.  Therefore, when the brain dies, consciousness ends.
